senses.gloss: Jabālā is the name of the mother of an illegitimate son, satyakāma, in the Chāndogya upaniṣad (iv. 4, 1. 2. 4).

Jābāla, ‘descendant of Jabāla,’ is the metronymic of mahāśāla and satyakāma. jābāla is also mentioned as a teacher in the Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa, which refers to the Jābālas as well. The jābāla Gṛhapatis are spoken of in the kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa.

Jābāla.--For ‘descendant of Jabāla’ read ‘descendant of jabālā.’

Jābālāyana, ‘descendant of jābāla,’ is the patronymic of a teacher, a pupil of mādhyaṃdināyana, who is mentioned in the second vaṃśa (list of teachers) of the kāṇva recension of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad (iv. 6, 2).
